pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, The Transfiguration — Christ standing in a white robe with His arms outstretched inside a tall pale oval of light, a red and gold cross halo behind His head, haloed apostles kneeling below Him in rose and white with one shielding his face, and a robed figure at each edge of the cracked fresco, then jesus said to them, truly i tell you, there are some standing here who will not taste death before they see the kingdom of god arrive with power, after six days jesus took with him peter, james, and john, and led them up a high mountain by themselves, there he was transfigured before them
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_the_transfiguration

pictures.scene: Philippe de Champaigne, Moses with the Ten Commandments — a white-bearded Moses in a blue velvet mantle over a gold-embroidered robe, two small horns of light at his brow, holding up a grey stone tablet lettered with the commandments while a gold rod rests under his hand, all against a black ground, his clothes became radiantly white, brighter than any launderer on earth could bleach them, and elijah and moses appeared before them, talking with jesus
pictures.name: pd_champaigne_moses_with_the_ten_commandments

pictures.scene: Georges de la Tour, The Adoration of the Shepherds — a candlelit night stable where four or five shepherds and a woman in a white headcloth lean in around a swaddled infant asleep in a straw basket, one hand cupped to shield the flame, an ox's head at the left and a crook and an earthenware bowl beside them, peter said to jesus, rabbi, it is good for us to be here, let us put up three shelters, one for you, one for moses, and one for elijah, for they were all so terrified that peter did not know what else to say
pictures.name: pd_latour_adoration_shepherds

pictures.scene: Francesco Botticini, The Assumption of the Virgin, heaven — ranks of kneeling angels in pink, blue and white with red and black wings on a gold ground, elders holding books and a red cross among them, and below a plain band of sky the apostles in blue, orange and rose crowding around an open white sarcophagus filled with lilies, then a cloud appeared and enveloped them, and a voice came from the cloud, this is my beloved son, listen to him, suddenly, when they looked around, they saw no one with them except jesus
pictures.name: pd_botticini_hemel

pictures.scene: Altobello Melone, The Road to Emmaus — two barefoot travellers walking a road, a bald white-bearded man in blue under a deep orange mantle raising his hand in the middle of an argument and a long-haired young man in green under a rose and crimson cloak striding beside him, with a walled hill town and small figures behind them, as they were coming down the mountain, jesus admonished them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the son of man had risen from the dead, so they kept this matter to themselves, discussing what it meant to rise from the dead
pictures.name: pd_melone_wandelt

pictures.scene: Salomon Koninck, The Old Philosopher — an old scholar in a fur-trimmed brown gown and a twisted orange turban bent over a large open white book on a carpet-covered table, a quill and loose papers at his elbow, in a dim brown room, and they asked jesus, why do the scribes say that elijah must come first, he replied, elijah does indeed come first, and he restores all things, why then is it written that the son of man must suffer many things and be rejected
pictures.name: pd_koninck_old_philosopher

pictures.scene: Max Liebermann, The Twelve-Year-Old Jesus in the Temple — a boy in a pale tunic seen from behind standing before seated elders in prayer shawls and black coats in a dim synagogue, one old man leaning forward with his hand at his mouth, more men reading at a bench above, and pale stone pavement underfoot, but i tell you that elijah has indeed come, and they have done to him whatever they wished, just as it is written about him, when they returned to the other disciples, they saw a large crowd around them, and scribes arguing with them
pictures.name: pd_liebermann_jesus_im_tempel

pictures.scene: Otto Eerelman, The Entry of Queen Wilhelmina into Amsterdam — a great crowd pressed along both sides of a cobbled avenue under a domed church and tall autumn trees, orange flags and a fountain playing behind them, plumed cavalry in gold-braided uniforms filling the middle of the street, and an open white carriage carrying two women in white at the centre of it all, as soon as all the people saw jesus, they were filled with awe and ran to greet him, what are you disputing with them, he asked
pictures.name: pd_eerelman_intocht_wilhelmina

pictures.scene: Adolph Tidemand, The Sick Child — a dim cottage interior lit by a single lamp on the left where a young mother in a striped headscarf and white sleeves sits with her hand at her mouth watching a small child lying wrapped in a basket cradle between them, and the father in a red waistcoat sits opposite with his arms folded, someone in the crowd replied, teacher, i brought you my son, who has a spirit that makes him mute, whenever it seizes him, it throws him to the ground, he foams at the mouth, gnashes his teeth, and becomes rigid, i asked your disciples to drive it out, but they were unable
pictures.name: pd_tidemand_het_zieke_kind

pictures.scene: Hans Andersen Brendekilde, Worn Out — an old labourer in a blue smock collapsed face up on the bare brown earth of a wide stony field with his hoe fallen beside him, and a woman in a red bodice and tan shawl on her knees over him, her mouth open, crying out across the empty furrows toward a far-off farm, o unbelieving generation, jesus replied, how long must i remain with you, how long must i put up with you, bring the boy to me, so they brought him, and seeing jesus, the spirit immediately threw the boy into a convulsion, he fell to the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth
pictures.name: pd_brendekilde_uitgeput

pictures.scene: John Everett Millais, The Rescue — a fireman in a black helmet and heavy coat striding out of the smoke of a burning house with two children in nightgowns gathered up in his arms, one slung over his shoulder, and their mother in a pale gown flung forward from the right to take the third child, with flames licking along the floor behind his boots, jesus asked the boy's father, how long has this been with him, from childhood, he said, it often throws him into the fire or into the water, trying to kill him, but if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us
pictures.name: pd_millais_the_rescue

pictures.scene: Gerrit Dou, A Hermit at Prayer — a bald old man with a white beard in a coarse brown habit with his hands folded together at his breast and a rosary of dark beads hanging between his fingers, a gilt crucifix lying on the table edge below, lit from the left against a dark stone niche, if you can, echoed jesus, all things are possible to him who believes, immediately the boy's father cried out, i do believe, help my unbelief
pictures.name: pd_dou_kluizenaar_in_gebed

pictures.scene: Gabriel Metsu, The Sick Child — a woman in a brown jacket and blue skirt seated against a pale wall with a listless child in a yellow jacket and white shift lying back across her lap, the child's legs hanging limp and its eyes turned out at the viewer, a map on a roller to the left and a dark-framed crucifixion picture on the wall above, when jesus saw that a crowd had come running, he rebuked the unclean spirit, you deaf and mute spirit, he said, i command you to come out and never enter him again, after shrieking and convulsing him violently, the spirit came out, the boy became like a corpse, so that many said, he is dead
pictures.name: pd_metsu_the_sick_child

pictures.scene: Jacob Willemsz de Wet, Christ Blessing the Children — a haloed Christ in a white robe and red mantle seated on a stone step inside a shadowed hall with His hand laid to His breast, mothers kneeling and pressing small children toward Him, a girl in a yellow dress kneeling with her hands joined at His feet, a boy in a red cap crouching in front of her, and bearded disciples standing behind, but jesus took him by the hand and helped him to his feet, and he stood up, after jesus had gone into the house, his disciples asked him privately, why couldn't we drive it out
pictures.name: pd_dewet_christus_zegent_kinderen

pictures.scene: Maurycy Gottlieb, Jews Praying in the Synagogue on Yom Kippur — a crowded synagogue where men in white and black striped prayer shawls stand pressed shoulder to shoulder, one carrying a Torah scroll in an embroidered mantle, another resting his head in his hand with his eyes shut, a boy in a flowered coat at the front, and women in headscarves leaning over the gallery rail above, jesus answered, this kind cannot come out, except by prayer, going on from there, they passed through galilee, but jesus did not want anyone to know
pictures.name: pd_gottlieb_jews_praying_on_yom_kippur

pictures.scene: Giotto, The Kiss of Judas — Christ standing still in a gold mantle while Judas wraps Him in a yellow cloak and leans in to kiss His face, a ring of helmeted soldiers in red and violet closing around the two of them, and clubs, spears and burning torches crossing the deep blue sky above their heads, because he was teaching his disciples, he told them, the son of man will be delivered into the hands of men, they will kill him, and after three days he will rise, but they did not understand this statement, and they were afraid to ask him about it
pictures.name: pd_giotto_the_kiss_of_judas

pictures.scene: Francois Marius Granet, The Chapter Meeting — a tall vaulted chapel in half darkness with a framed altarpiece hung high on the end wall and rows of dark paintings down both side walls, monks in hooded habits seated along the wooden choir stalls on either side, and a few small figures standing out on the bare lit floor between them, then they came to capernaum, while jesus was in the house, he asked them, what were you discussing on the way, but they were silent, for on the way they had been arguing about which of them was the greatest
pictures.name: pd_granet_vergadering

pictures.scene: Albert Neuhuys, Mother and Child — a peasant woman in a dull green jacket and a white cap seated on a rush chair in a brown cottage with a fair-haired baby in a white shift held on her lap, the child turning a small rattle in its fist, one clog still on its foot, and a basket of mending on the table at the left, sitting down, jesus called the twelve and said, if anyone wants to be first, he must be the last of all and the servant of all, then he had a little child stand among them, taking the child in his arms, he said to them
pictures.name: pd_neuhuys_moeder_en_kind

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Jacob Blessing the Children of Joseph — an old man in a white gown propped up in bed laying his right hand on the fair head of a kneeling boy while Joseph in a great pale turban reaches to move the hand gently across, a dark-haired younger boy looking up from the foot of the bed, and Joseph's wife in a brown gown standing at the right above a deep red coverlet, whoever welcomes one of these little children in my name welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes not only me, but the one who sent me, john said to him, teacher, we saw someone else driving out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not accompany us
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_jacob_blessing_the_children_of_joseph

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Census at Bethlehem — a snow-covered Flemish village at sunset with one great bare tree rising through the middle of the picture, villagers crowding at the window of an inn to be registered under a wreath and a coat of arms, a frozen river full of skaters behind, and in front men sawing timber, a woman carrying a basket, a cart wheel and two chickens on the trodden snow, do not stop him, jesus replied, for no one who performs a miracle in my name can turn around and speak evil of me, for whoever is not against us is for us
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_volkstelling

pictures.scene: Guercino, Christ at the Well — a bearded Christ in a red robe and dark blue mantle leaning both hands on the stone rim of a well, His lips parted in speech and His head turned up and away to the right, with a single tree and a dim evening sky behind Him, indeed, if anyone gives you even a cup of water because you bear the name of christ, truly i tell you, he will never lose his reward, but if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea
pictures.name: pd_guercino_christ_at_the_well

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Cripples — a group of beggars in white smocks hung with foxtails moving on short wooden crutches across a patch of grass beside a brick wall, one of them kneeling on padded stumps with his back turned, another lifting his face and crying out, and a woman in a black cloak walking away behind them with an empty bowl, if your hand causes you to sin, cut it off, it is better for you to enter life crippled than to have two hands and go into hell, into the unquenchable fire, if your foot causes you to sin, cut it off, it is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into hell
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_beggars

pictures.scene: Peder Severin Kroyer, Midsummer Eve Bonfire on Skagen Beach — a huge bonfire throwing a sheet of flame sideways into the blue dusk, men in work clothes feeding it with a long pole, women in white summer dresses and straw hats watching from the far side, and in front of it children seated on the firelit sand and two boys standing dark against the glow with their arms around each other, and if your eye causes you to sin, pluck it out, it is better for you to enter the kingdom of god with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell, where their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched
pictures.name: pd_kroyer_midsummer_eve_bonfire

pictures.scene: Jean-Francois Millet, The Angelus — a peasant woman in a dark dress and hood standing alone in a ploughed field at dusk with her head bowed and her hands clasped at her breast, a basket of potatoes at her feet and a wooden barrow behind her, and a distant church spire on the flat horizon under a heavy evening sky, for everyone will be salted with fire, salt is good, but if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it, have salt among yourselves, and be at peace with one another
pictures.name: pd_millet_the_angelus

lines.text: Then Jesus said to them, Truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God arrive with power.
After six days Jesus took with Him Peter, James, and John, and led them up a high mountain by themselves. There He was transfigured before them.
His clothes became radiantly white, brighter than any launderer on earth could bleach them.
And Elijah and Moses appeared before them, talking with Jesus.
Peter said to Jesus, Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters, one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.
For they were all so terrified that Peter did not know what else to say.
Then a cloud appeared and enveloped them, and a voice came from the cloud: This is My beloved Son. Listen to Him!
Suddenly, when they looked around, they saw no one with them except Jesus.
As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus admonished them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
So they kept this matter to themselves, discussing what it meant to rise from the dead.
And they asked Jesus, Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?
He replied, Elijah does indeed come first, and he restores all things. Why then is it written that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected?
But I tell you that Elijah has indeed come, and they have done to him whatever they wished, just as it is written about him.
When they returned to the other disciples, they saw a large crowd around them, and scribes arguing with them.
As soon as all the people saw Jesus, they were filled with awe and ran to greet Him.
What are you disputing with them? He asked.
Someone in the crowd replied, Teacher, I brought You my son, who has a spirit that makes him mute.
Whenever it seizes him, it throws him to the ground. He foams at the mouth, gnashes his teeth, and becomes rigid. I asked Your disciples to drive it out, but they were unable.
O unbelieving generation! Jesus replied. How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy to Me.
So they brought him, and seeing Jesus, the spirit immediately threw the boy into a convulsion. He fell to the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth.
Jesus asked the boy's father, How long has this been with him? From childhood, he said.
It often throws him into the fire or into the water, trying to kill him. But if You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.
If You can? echoed Jesus. All things are possible to him who believes!
Immediately the boy's father cried out, I do believe; help my unbelief!
When Jesus saw that a crowd had come running, He rebuked the unclean spirit. You deaf and mute spirit, He said, I command you to come out and never enter him again.
After shrieking and convulsing him violently, the spirit came out. The boy became like a corpse, so that many said, He is dead.
But Jesus took him by the hand and helped him to his feet, and he stood up.
After Jesus had gone into the house, His disciples asked Him privately, Why couldn't we drive it out?
Jesus answered, This kind cannot come out, except by prayer.
Going on from there, they passed through Galilee. But Jesus did not want anyone to know,
because He was teaching His disciples. He told them, The Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men. They will kill Him, and after three days He will rise.
But they did not understand this statement, and they were afraid to ask Him about it.
Then they came to Capernaum. While Jesus was in the house, He asked them, What were you discussing on the way?
But they were silent, for on the way they had been arguing about which of them was the greatest.
Sitting down, Jesus called the Twelve and said, If anyone wants to be first, he must be the last of all and the servant of all.
Then He had a little child stand among them. Taking the child in His arms, He said to them,
Whoever welcomes one of these little children in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes not only Me, but the One who sent Me.
John said to Him, Teacher, we saw someone else driving out demons in Your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not accompany us.
Do not stop him, Jesus replied. For no one who performs a miracle in My name can turn around and speak evil of Me.
For whoever is not against us is for us.
Indeed, if anyone gives you even a cup of water because you bear the name of Christ, truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward.
But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea.
If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life crippled than to have two hands and go into hell, into the unquenchable fire.
If your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into hell.
And if your eye causes you to sin, pluck it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell,
where their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched.
For everyone will be salted with fire.
Salt is good, but if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt among yourselves, and be at peace with one another.
